limitations: visible_complete is controller completion, not independent final acceptance. Passing every active case does not establish correctness on unexecuted requirements.
Reviewer notes and requirement labels are model assertions. The memo separates them from actual matrix outcomes; it does not endorse prose claims merely because they were stated.
Raw physical stage receipts are matched to freeze-bound controller evidence; this is not a replacement for the independent full journal/runtime/receipt audit.
A bounded stop can expose a scheduling or evidence bottleneck, but no counterfactual continuation was executed. Additional repairs or stronger routing are hypotheses, not claimed rescues.

Exact-source changes can reset the controller stagnation signal even when the same failures remain; newly admitted passing tests can also count as progress. Hard review/repair ceilings remain binding.
No comparison of policy superiority, model skill, private correctness, or cross-policy test quality is made here.
method: Verify all ten trajectory byte hashes and all seventeen stage-result byte hashes against the global provider freeze.
Verify source exports and selected source hashes without importing or executing candidate code.
Read exact freeze-bound reviewer and repair requests; distinguish their pre-decision evidence from tests proposed in the same response.

Match public/probe matrices to retained physical stage receipts on exact source, case identity and typed actual/pass/status projection. Recompute passing and wrong-answer comparisons with canonical JSON types; executed error rows remain failures without inventing a wrong-answer value.
Match embedded initial/final candidate validation receipts to exact physical receipt objects. Multiple matching historical observations are listed as support, not counted as independent defects.
Compare repair failures only on the same active cases supplied in that repair request; changed-source counts are not evidence of improved quality.
Re-read every captured input at handoff to reject changing evidence. No new model call, candidate execution, candidate private evaluation or primary-result mutation.
scope: Frozen controller behavior and actually executed public/oracle-admitted probe evidence only. No final/private receipts, fault bank, cross-policy grading, mutable study results, or mutable timing files were read.
status: public-controller observations; primary acceptance audit owned by root and not incorporated

repair_same_case_comparison.meaning: Each comparison uses exactly the active cases supplied in that repair request. Counts do not equate source novelty with improvement or compare differently expanded suites.

reviews.reviewer_notes: candidate-C is the strongest retained source: it passes all legacy B1-B4 evidence and all exercised G1 cases except graph-extension-s1-rename-basic. In that failing case it returns invalidated:[] after renaming dirty a->z with dependent b, but the requirement says rename must report all affected IDs, including nodes already dirty, when their dependency list or dependency bindings changed; b should be listed because its deps rewrite from [a] to [z]. Audit/history behavior for that case is otherwise aligned, including rename event ids ["a","b","z"]. Repair only candidate-C's rename invalidation computation so response invalidated includes affected already-dirty nodes while still not spuriously adding unaffected pre-existing dirty nodes.

candidate-D is the strongest retained source. It passes all exercised legacy B1-B4 cases and the G1 validation/retry/history checks, including graph-extension-s1-rename-stale, graph-extension-s1-rename-types, and the self-map replay case. However it still fails the exercised rename cache/simultaneous semantics: in graph-extension-s1-rename-basic and graph-patch:881820d... it returns invalidated:["b"] and audit ids ["b"], but the trusted expectation requires invalidated:["b"] with changed-id audit ids ["a","b","z"]. In graph-patch:16847d... it returns invalidated:[] and audit ids [], but swapping built roots under fan-in c must invalidate c while audit ids remain only ["a","b"]. Repair only candidate-D's rename handling so it computes two distinct sets correctly: (1) response invalidated = newly affected nodes in the final graph whose source/dependency list or dependency bindings changed, plus their reverse dependents, excluding unaffected pre-existing dirty nodes; (2) audit changed ids = union of old/new names whose records differ by source/priority/deps or are absent on one side, ignoring digest/provenance. Preserve digest retention for unchanged renamed roots and existing replay/version behavior.

candidate-D is the strongest retained source: it passes all exercised B1-B4 requirements and the G1 validation/retry/history checks, while candidate-B errors broadly and candidates A/C fail the same rename semantics with additional stale/basic over-invalidation. However executed evidence already shows candidate-D is not yet admissible for acceptance on rename cache/simultaneous behavior. In graph-extension-s1-rename-basic and graph-patch:881820dbe60431af8abfa49986dd997ff3789fc301b03dc92ae17241ae3fa93f it returns invalidated ["b","z"] instead of only ["b"], so the unchanged renamed root z is being reported as newly affected. In graph-extension-s1-rename-stale it returns invalidated ["z"] instead of [], showing the same issue for a dirty renamed root. In graph-patch:16847d95bb7f0dc8a22c35f1bfbc3d83587083d272c3367a543cca2056a6118b it returns invalidated ["a","b","c"] instead of only ["c"], so swapping built roots under a fan-in is incorrectly treated as affecting the renamed roots rather than only the dependent whose bindings changed. Another review should run after probes targeting rename invalidation vs durable audit/history distinctions.

candidate-D remains the best retained source: it passes the exercised legacy B1-B4 matrix and G1 validation/retry/history checks, while candidate-B errors broadly and candidates A/C additionally over-invalidate rename results. However candidate-D still fails the executed rename cache semantics required for acceptance. In graph-extension-s1-rename-basic and graph-patch:881820dbe60431af8abfa49986dd997ff3789fc301b03dc92ae17241ae3fa93f, renaming dirty a->z with dependent b incorrectly reports invalidated ["b","z"]; the expected result is only ["b"], so an unchanged renamed root is being treated as newly affected. In graph-extension-s1-rename-stale, the successful replayed rename response still includes invalidated ["z"] instead of [], confirming the same root over-invalidation is persisted in receipts. In graph-patch:16847d95bb7f0dc8a22c35f1bfbc3d83587083d272c3367a543cca2056a6118b, swapping built roots a<->b under fan-in c returns invalidated ["a","b","c"] instead of only ["c"], so simultaneous rename is not preserving root digests when source and literal dependency IDs stay unchanged and only downstream dependency bindings change. Acceptance is not admissible because remaining requirements are non-empty.

reviews.reviewer_notes: All executed cases for every alias show status=error, and candidate-D has a concrete fatal source issue: buildgraph_app/service.py constructs dict(from=...) in rename responses, which is invalid Python syntax and prevents any scenario from running. Candidate-D is the strongest repair base because it already carries provenance through storage/service, normalizes rename requests for durable replay/conflict, checks replay before stale/state checks, and preserves legacy command structure. Repair candidate-D by fixing the syntax error, then tighten rename semantics: keep audit ids as changed IDs only (not full reverse-dependent invalidation closure), keep invalidated as affected final-node IDs, preserve digests only when dependency bindings still denote the original nodes, and ensure dirty preexisting nodes are not spuriously counted as newly affected solely because they were already dirty. Re-review after repair and probe execution.

Repair candidate-D only: replace those constructions with JSON-safe literal dicts like {'from': ..., 'to': ...}; then re-review against the full matrix. After syntax repair, pay special attention to G1 replay canonicalization and provenance-sensitive digest preservation for rename, because acceptance requires the rename path to preserve prior milestones and the shared durable key namespace behavior.

The other candidates have uniform status=error across the matrix, so they are not eligible for acceptance over the evidenced source. candidate-D is source_valid=true and remaining requirements are fully discharged by the passed evidence.
